Menus

The main menu, the settings, the map of the scroll and the journal, in the same style as the game. The font is the game's Old Fax, which now includes drawn arrows and a middle dot. Each has the deep-papyrus title bar with its band, and the scribe's strip. Each frame works: click through the main menu, scroll the map with the wheel and click its scenes, and change the settings.

Main menu

A · Over the scene

The game's own frame: title bar, band and scribe strip, with the menu sheet beside Ra and his adorer.

B · Title page

A book's title page. The band frames the whole screen, with Ra and his adorer as a frontispiece and the title in large letters. The four items are buttons in a 2×2 grid; Continue is filled red.

C · In the scene

No panel. The items hang as red tags over figures of the scroll, like the speaker's tag on the band: Settings over Ra, Continue over his adorer, the scroll over the tomb.

D · Ink

Dark ink with cream type; one length of the band under the title; the scene as a framed papyrus card.

The scroll (map and progress)

A · The register

Every scene on one register of the scroll, reading right to left, between its double rules; the acts captioned above.

B · Senet board

The scenes as the squares of a senet board, four rows of six, the path snaking right to left and back, ending in the West. Each square is filled by its picture, with its number and spells beneath. Restored squares carry an ankh, the pawn stands on the current one, and squares ahead show only a faint imprint. The chosen square opens in the strip below.

C · Contents

A book's table of contents over two spreads, turned with the arrows: Acts I–III, then Acts IV to the Finale. Each scene has a miniature of its vignette, a dotted leader and its spells. Restored scenes are marked with an ankh and the current one with the pawn; scenes ahead are pale. The chosen line's miniature is outlined in red, and the scene is described under the book.

D · Plates

A wall of plates, act by act under lengths of the band, each row reading right to left. The chosen plate opens in the strip below.

Settings

Minimal

Four rows: one sound volume, fullscreen, the controls, and beginning again. Text size, scaling and motion are decided by the game.

Journal

A · Framed

The journal lists each entry by its name, with its figure as a small icon, the newest first. Clicking a name opens the entry on the page beside the list: the figure, the name and the whole description. The next row peeks out under the last one to show the list scrolls. The sheet's border is ink, dark red, ink, and the scribe's strip is hidden while the journal is open. Icons and the page's figure sit in dark-papyrus frames with an ink outline.

B · No frames

The same page, with the figures drawn straight on the papyrus: no darker ground and no outline around the icons or the page's figure. The page's figure stands on a single line, its own groundline carried across the whole column. The double rule runs out to the border, the groundline runs across to the divider and the border, and a rule runs between every entry from the border to the divider. The chosen entry is shown only by its name in red.

C · No frames, 6px lines

B with every line drawn 6px thick: the double rule, the divider, the rules between entries, the groundline and the three rings of the border. The double rule has an 8px gap between its lines.

D · Page and strip

The sizes of B (4px lines, a double rule with a 4px gap). The chosen entry fills the page: its title and description on the left, its figure larger on the right, standing on its groundline carried across to the divider and the border. Under it, a row of icons, with no titles and no rules between them, in the order they come on the scroll, which reads right to left, so the first sits at the right edge; the wheel moves the row sideways. The chosen icon is boxed in red. The border is ink, yellow, ink, and the icons are all the same height, so each is as wide as its figure's proportions make it.

F · Page and strip, icons to scale

D, but the icons are not stretched to one height: every figure is drawn at the same scale, so each keeps its real size next to the others, and they all stand on the same bottom line. The tallest figure (Osiris enthroned) is 64px high, and the wide boats and baboons run wider and shorter.

G · Strip under the title

F with the double rule moved. It no longer sits under the title: the row of icons comes straight after the title, the double rule runs under the row, and the page (title and description, divider, figure) fills the rest down to the border. The divider starts at the double rule.

E · Page and strip, 6px lines

D with every line drawn 6px thick: the double rule (with an 8px gap), the divider, the rule above the icons, the groundline and the box around the chosen icon. The icons are the same height and as wide as their proportions make them. The border is ink, an 8px band of yellow (the hint yellow), ink.
